paper_title: MMAR A Challenging Benchmark for Deep Reasoning in Speech, Audio,   Music, and Their Mix
caption: : Compare with noise input on MMAR
model_annotation: The bar chart compares the accuracy (%) of three models—Qwen2-Audio-Instruct, Audio-Reasoner, and Qwen-2.5-Omni—when given either audio input or noise input, as part of the MMAR benchmark for deep reasoning in speech, audio, and music. The horizontal axis lists the three models in left-to-right order, while the vertical axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 0 to 60 with major tick marks at intervals of 10. For each model, two bars are shown: a solid blue bar for "Audio" input and a solid purple bar for "Noise" input, as indicated in the legend. A dashed horizontal line at 30% represents the "Random Choice" baseline. The blue bars (Audio) are consistently higher than the purple bars (Noise) across all models, indicating better performance with audio input. Specifically, Qwen2-Audio-Instruct achieves approximately 32% accuracy with audio and 24% with noise; Audio-Reasoner reaches about 38% with audio and 32% with noise; and Qwen-2.5-Omni attains roughly 55% with audio and 36% with noise. The bars are arranged in groups by model, with no stacking, and are not sorted by height. The chart visually emphasizes the performance gap between audio and noise inputs, with all audio bars exceeding the random choice baseline, while noise bars are mostly close to or slightly above it.
